description: Common technique faults with fixes, and stop rules.

tags.Well supported: Consistent findings across reviews or a position stand.
tags.Moderate: Supported, but limited by study size, population or design.
tags.Standard practice: Widely used convention without strong direct evidence.
tags.Contested: Published evidence disagrees or is thin; Gideon should say so.
tags.Library design: A deliberate choice in how these plans are built.
tags.Definition: Plain-language meaning of a term used in the app.

S1.title: ACSM Position Stand: Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults (2026)
S1.note: Read through a mirror PDF, about the first 100,000 of 122,000 characters.

S2.title: The Resistance Training Dose-Response: Meta-Regressions on Weekly Volume and Frequency (Sports Medicine, 2025)
S2.note: 67 studies, 79% male, mostly young adults, about 10 weeks.

S3.title: Gaining more from doing less? One-week deload during supervised resistance training (PeerJ, 2024)
S3.note: 39 trained adults; tested a full week off, not reduced volume.

S4.title: Much Ado About Zone 2 (Sports Medicine, 2025)
S4.note: Narrative review; few trials prescribed Zone 2 directly.

S5.title: Concurrent strength and endurance training: systematic review and meta-analysis (Sports Medicine, 2023)

S6.title: Factors influencing the accuracy of the repetition in reserve scale in resistance training: a systematic review (Russo et al., 2025)
S6.note: Abstract and headings only were read.

S7.title: World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
S7.note: Excerpt did not give the muscle-strengthening frequency.

S8.title: Stretching in healthy athletes: systematic scoping review and evidence gap map (Sports Medicine, 2024)
S8.note: Evidence map of 300 trials, not a pooled analysis.

S9.title: ACE: Nutrition Scope of Practice, What You Can Do as a Personal Trainer

S10.title: NSCA-Certified Personal Trainer exam description
S10.note: Domain weights: consultation and assessment 23%, program planning 29%, program execution 36%, safety and legal 12%.

S11.note: Title and search listing only; full text not read.

S12.note: Title and search listing only; full text not read.

faults.looksLike: Knees drift toward each other on the way up.
faults.fix: Lighten the load, push the knees out over the toes, and pause at the bottom.

faults.fault: Heels lift or torso falls forward
faults.looksLike: Weight shifts to the toes and the chest drops.
faults.fix: Elevate the heels slightly, brace before descending, and keep the whole foot planted.

faults.looksLike: The back rounds and the weight pulls the chest down.
faults.fix: Keep the weight tight to the chest, sit between the hips and reduce depth until it stays tall.

faults.fault: Bar drifts away from the legs
faults.looksLike: The bar swings forward and the lower back takes the load.
faults.fix: Keep the bar over the mid-foot and brush the legs; squeeze the armpits down before pulling.

faults.looksLike: The back flexes as the bar leaves the floor.
faults.fix: Lighten the load, brace first, and stop the set when the back changes shape.

faults.looksLike: Knees bend a lot and hips stay low.
faults.fix: Soft knees only, push the hips back as if closing a door, and feel the hamstrings load.

faults.fault: Overarching the lower back at the top
faults.looksLike: Ribs flare up and the lower back pinches.
faults.fix: Tuck the ribs down, tilt the pelvis slightly, and finish with the glutes, not the back.

faults.fault: Lifting with the arms or squatting it
faults.looksLike: The bell rises from the arms and the knees bend deeply.
faults.fix: Hinge back, snap the hips forward and keep the arms loose like ropes.

faults.fault: Bouncing the bar or lifting the hips
faults.looksLike: The bar rebounds off the chest and the hips rise.
faults.fix: Lower under control, pause briefly and keep feet planted and shoulder blades pulled back.

faults.fault: Wrists bent back and elbows flared
faults.looksLike: Dumbbells tilt and elbows point straight out.
faults.fix: Stack the wrist over the elbow and tuck the elbows to about 45 degrees.

faults.looksLike: The body is not in one line.
faults.fix: Squeeze the glutes and abs, keep ribs down, and use a higher surface if needed.

faults.looksLike: The ribs flare and the lower back arches to finish the rep.
faults.fix: Squeeze the glutes, keep the ribs down and lower the weight to what moves cleanly.

faults.looksLike: The torso swings to move the weight.
faults.fix: Hold the hinge position, pull the elbow toward the hip and reduce the load.

faults.looksLike: The chin never clears the bar or the legs swing.
faults.fix: Start from a full hang, pull the chest toward the bar, and step down to Lat Pulldown or Inverted Row until reps are clean.

faults.fault: Leaning far back or pulling behind the neck
faults.looksLike: The torso rocks and the bar goes behind the head.
faults.fix: Lean back slightly, pull the bar to the upper chest, and drive the elbows down.

faults.fault: Front knee caves or torso tilts
faults.looksLike: The front knee drifts in and the trunk leans.
faults.fix: Shorten the stance slightly, push the knee over the toes and keep the torso tall.

faults.looksLike: The weight shifts to the toes.
faults.fix: Take a slightly longer step and press through the whole front foot.

faults.looksLike: The trailing leg does the work.
faults.fix: Drive through the front heel and keep the trailing foot light.

faults.looksLike: The shoulders ride up and the weight swings.
faults.fix: Use a light load, keep elbows high and pull the rope apart toward the ears.

faults.looksLike: The torso rocks to lift the weights.
faults.fix: Lighten the load, lead with the elbows and lift only to shoulder height.

faults.looksLike: The back leans to start the lift.
faults.fix: Pin the elbows at the sides and lower the bar slowly.

faults.looksLike: The elbows drift forward and the shoulders hunch.
faults.fix: Pin the elbows at the sides and keep the shoulders down.

faults.fault: Hips sag or pike, or holding the breath
faults.looksLike: The body is not straight and breathing stops.
faults.fix: Ribs down, glutes tight, breathe slowly, and end the set when the hips sag.

faults.looksLike: The back lifts off the floor as the legs lower.
faults.fix: Press the low back down and shorten the range until it stays flat.

faults.looksLike: The hips twist as the leg reaches back.
faults.fix: Keep the hips level as if balancing a cup on the lower back; move slowly.

faults.looksLike: The body tilts to one side and steps are tiny.
faults.fix: Stand tall, ribs down, and take smooth steady steps.

faults.looksLike: The landing is loud and the knees collapse.
faults.fix: Land softly, reset between reps and lower the jump height.

faults.looksLike: Landing off the box stresses the legs and Achilles.
faults.fix: Step down every time and pick a lower box.

faults.fault: Sagging push-up or arched back on the jump
faults.looksLike: The hips drop in the plank and the back arches.
faults.fix: Keep the body straight in the push-up position and slow the pace.

faults.looksLike: The press does all the work.
faults.fix: Drive from the legs, time the press with the squat's upward drive and use a lighter load.

faults.fault: Shoulders roll forward or too deep
faults.looksLike: The chest collapses and the shoulders feel pinched.
faults.fix: Keep the shoulders down, stop at a depth that feels comfortable and step down to Close-Grip Bench Press if needed.

faults.fault: Lower back rounds off the pad or knees lock out
faults.looksLike: The hips curl under at the bottom and the knees snap straight.
faults.fix: Shorten the depth and keep a slight knee bend at the top.

faults.looksLike: The rep uses momentum, not the calf.
faults.fix: Pause at the bottom stretch and lift with control.

faults.looksLike: The back arches instead of the hips lifting.
faults.fix: Tuck the ribs, press the heels down and squeeze the glutes.

faults.fault: Letting the knees fall too far
faults.looksLike: The hips shift and the feet slide.
faults.fix: Keep the soles together, find a comfortable knee angle and squeeze at the top.

faults.looksLike: One side of the pelvis sags.
faults.fix: Keep the hips level and use the two-leg version until even.

faults.looksLike: The knee drops in as the other foot reaches down.
faults.fix: Use a lower step, slow the lowering and keep the knee over the toes.

faults.looksLike: The torso rocks and the legs swing.
faults.fix: Use a lighter pad, pause at the end of the range and keep the back against the pad.

stopRules.stopWhen: Chest pain or pressure during exercise
stopRules.whatGideonSays: Tell them to stop, sit down and rest. If pain does not clear quickly or you suspect an emergency, call local emergency services. Do not diagnose.

stopRules.stopWhen: Dizziness, fainting, or severe shortness of breath
stopRules.whatGideonSays: Tell them to stop and sit or lie down. Recommend medical care. Do not continue the program discussion until they confirm they are okay.

stopRules.stopWhen: Sudden sharp pain, popping, or a joint that gives way
stopRules.whatGideonSays: Stop the movement. Suggest rest and a clinician if pain persists. Offer the app's general alternates for later, not as treatment.

stopRules.stopWhen: Numbness, tingling or loss of coordination
stopRules.whatGideonSays: Stop and recommend medical care. Do not diagnose.

stopRules.stopWhen: Pain that is getting worse across sets
stopRules.whatGideonSays: Stop that movement, offer the alternate and suggest a clinician if it continues.

stopRules.stopWhen: Pressure, doming in the belly or leaking during core work
stopRules.whatGideonSays: Pause the set and use an easier version. If it keeps happening, suggest a pelvic health clinician.

stopRules.stopWhen: Any sign of a medical emergency
stopRules.whatGideonSays: Say plainly to call local emergency services. Do not offer training advice in that message.

emergencyNote: For any emergency, Gideon says to call local emergency services and offers no training advice in that message.
